title: Profile the residual BitVec shift family
description:
Establish the separate workload profile and materiality disposition for arbitrary-offset zero-fill `BitVec` shifts without changing production code or authorizing an ISA-specific implementation.

## Background

`BitVec::shift_left` and `BitVec::shift_right` dispatch whole-word offsets through the canonical backend while residual offsets use safe scalar carry loops. The repository-wide consumer sweep finds no downstream production caller, so this work measures the public primitive as an isolated family and records whole-consumer measurement as inapplicable rather than inventing a consumer. The profile uses release builds on the prepared Zen 3 host under protocol version 4 and keeps the existing word-shift path as a control.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A frozen protocol-v4 addendum and append-only family-ledger reservation predeclare the workload matrix, exploratory role, semantic oracle, cache states, measurement settings and bounded search before any timing starts.
- [hard] REQ-02: Scheduled benchmark-window execution produces an accepted exploratory receipt with exact rebuilt source and executable pins, raw paired samples, append-only execution log, checkpoints, runtime provenance and durable negative or unavailable outcomes.
- [hard] REQ-03: The semantic fixture corpus covers lengths and offsets 0, 1, 7, 8, 63, 64 and 65, offsets at and beyond the vector length, vector-lane crossings and incomplete final words; every result matches an independent zero-fill reference with zero tail padding.
- [hard] REQ-04: The report names the complete production consumer result, records the absence of a downstream production caller, separates the word-aligned control from residual work and makes no production-adoption claim.
- [hard] REQ-05: A no-candidate or no-win disposition permits this profile to complete. If it nominates a material AVX2 lane-crossing or BMI-based form, this profile remains open until a planning-time Rust 1.95 compile and assembly record proves feasibility, including a runtime-gated scalar fallback for any capability-gated form, and the plan bracket is amended and re-reviewed to create the required candidate implementation and confirmation leaves, make them depend on this profile, and re-home publication behind their sinks in the instantiated dependency graph.

## Notes

Follow `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md` and `dev/active/f547c394/protocol.md`. Timed work runs only in a scheduled benchmark window.

planning.outcome: Residual-shift materiality has a protocol-complete disposition

terminal.test_boundary: Independent acceptance re-evaluation against the pinned zero-fill fixture corpus
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One isolated operation family reuses the canonical campaign tooling with a bounded workload matrix

title: Route residual BitVec shifts through a BMI2-gated funnel kernel
description:
Dispatch the residual, non-word-aligned branch of the public `BitVec` shifts to a BMI2-gated funnel kernel, with the present scalar funnel as the tested fallback.

## Background

`BitVec::shift_left` and `BitVec::shift_right` consult the SIMD kernel bundle only when the offset is a whole number of words; a non-zero residual falls straight into a safe scalar double-word funnel. The residual-shift workload profile at `dev/active/c04dd4ac-zen3-shifts-and-permutations/shift-profile.md` records that branch as material at consequential sizes under its frozen rule and nominates two forms. The planning-time record at `dev/active/c04dd4ac-zen3-shifts-and-permutations/shift-feasibility-record.md` establishes both as feasible at the repository's Rust 1.95 floor and ranks the BMI2-gated scalar funnel first: it reaches its intended instructions from the expression the production loop already writes, so it costs a target-feature scope and a runtime gate rather than a new algorithm. That record is the source for which expression the compiler lowers to which instruction at that floor, for the six-bit count mask the 128-bit double-precision form needs, and for the absence of a double-precision shift intrinsic in `core::arch::x86_64` there; read it rather than re-deriving them. The nominated AVX2 lane-crossing funnel is feasible and is not selected for implementation here.

The kernel crate publishes one capability-gated bundle per kernel family, each with its own detection and its own safe wrappers, and `gf2-core` reaches each through its own accessor in the module its `simd` feature compiles. The residual funnel follows that shape rather than joining the AVX2-gated logical bundle, so a host that reports the capability without AVX2 still reaches the route. The family has no downstream production caller: the two public methods are the route's only consumers, and whether the route stays in production is decided by the frozen rule of its A/B confirmation rather than after the fact.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The funnel kernel lives in `gf2-kernels-simd` and carries an explicit safety contract at every unsafe boundary and at the target-feature scope it needs; no other production crate gains unsafe code.
- [hard] REQ-02: The residual branch of both public shift methods consults the funnel bundle's accessor behind the same non-default `simd` cargo feature the word-aligned branch uses, and the route is selected by its own `is_x86_feature_detected!` result rather than by another capability's gate.
- [hard] REQ-03: A host or build without the capability runs the present scalar funnel, and a test drives that fallback as a reachable route instead of assuming it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Both routes run one shared behavioural suite: the existing `BitVec` shift tests extended with the feasibility corpus shape, covering lengths and offsets 0, 1, 7, 8, 63, 64 and 65, offsets at and beyond the length, and sizes leaving an incomplete final word; every result matches an independent zero-fill reference over canonical little-endian indices and keeps zero tail padding.
- [hard] REQ-05: One selection point chooses the route, a lane witness reports the route that executed, and a force switch holds callers on the scalar funnel; the witness and the switch compile under the crate's `test-support` feature as well as under test, so one shipped measurement build drives either route, and each test that toggles them serializes its whole toggle-execute-observe-restore section under one mutex, following `crates/gf2-core/tests/prime_route_dispatch.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-06: The crates build and the shared suite passes on Rust 1.95, and a regenerated annotated release-build assembly artefact under the kernel crate's `x86/asm/<module>.asm.txt` convention shows the emitted loop of the dispatched path in both directions.
- [hard] REQ-07: Rustdoc on the dispatched path names the cargo feature that enables it and the runtime capability it requires, and states each unsafe boundary's safety condition.
- [hard] REQ-08: The retention-or-removal rule is on record before the route is measured: the route ships in order to be measured, its confirmation's frozen rule decides whether it stays or gives way to the scalar funnel, and this work publishes no speed claim of its own.

## Notes

`dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md` states the MSRV, scalar-fallback and unsafe-isolation requirements this work inherits. Nothing here is timed.

planning.outcome: Residual BitVec shifts run a BMI2-gated funnel kernel behind runtime detection

terminal.test_boundary: The shared BitVec shift behavioural suite run once per selected route
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One gated kernel with its dispatch branch reuses the existing shift suite extended by a pinned corpus shape

title: Confirm the BMI2 residual shift route against the scalar funnel
description:
Measure the shipped BMI2-gated residual shift route against the scalar funnel the library takes without it, as a protocol-version-4 A/B family with a pilot and a confirmation, and publish the receipts and the decision.

## Background

The residual-shift workload profile at `dev/active/c04dd4ac-zen3-shifts-and-permutations/shift-profile.md` records the residual branch as material against a word-aligned control that performs strictly less work per word, so no row of it supports adoption. This family answers the question it leaves open by comparing residual against residual at the cells that profile records as material. Both arms are the same shipped executable separated by the test-build lane switch: the baseline arm holds the residual branch on the scalar funnel and the candidate arm lets the gated route run, so the comparison isolates the dispatched route and nothing else. The family has no downstream production caller, so whole-consumer measurement is inapplicable and the public primitive is measured in isolation. This candidate is its own protocol family with its own append-only ledger, and the exploratory profile's receipt is context it pins by path and digest rather than evidence it inherits. The frozen rule decides retention, so a non-qualifying outcome removes the dispatched route instead of keeping it on a later argument.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A frozen family addendum is committed before the pilot launches, with every numeric setting from it and the shared protocol settings, and the confirmation addendum is derived from the committed pilot receipt by the repository's canonical confirmation freezer, with its derivation record beside it and a family description that states the confirmatory stage rather than the pilot's exploratory one.
- [hard] REQ-02: Both arms are the same shipped executable separated by the test-build lane switch, the baseline arm held on the scalar funnel and the candidate arm on the gated route, and each cell's selected route is recorded at run time.
- [hard] REQ-03: The pilot's cells are material cells of the residual-shift workload profile in both shift directions, and the confirmation retains as many of them as this family's confirmatory budget admits under the protocol's P-20 rule recomputed from the campaign-support sources for this family's own ledger; the derivation record names which cells are retained, which are dropped and why, and a ledger history admitting no confirmatory cell records that arithmetic as the outcome.
- [hard] REQ-04: The family's append-only ledger opens empty, records each attempt's reservation and is never hand-edited; an attempt aborted for a procedural defect in its own freeze or launch, before any result is read, is recorded under the voided-attempt rule with its stage preserved.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every arm and case operation passes a non-timed harness smoke before any timed campaign is queued: the smoke drives each arm with the benchmark runner's own transport encoder and framing, pins its request mirror against the runner's request in a test and records zero timing windows.
- [hard] REQ-06: Every timed run is a committed queue line for the benchmark window rather than a session launch, and an interrupted campaign resumes under its own identity without repeating a completed cell.
- [hard] REQ-07: Each campaign is verified from its own execution log: the declared cell count starts, checkpoints and completes exactly once, every cell reaches its declared pair count with a measured status, the campaign ends in a terminal complete record, and the acceptance tool recomputes the committed verdict.
- [hard] REQ-08: The published outcome states the verdict the acceptance summary records for each cell, including any not-material or regressed cell, and states how the verdict relates to the exploratory profile receipt it pins by path and digest as context; a non-qualifying outcome is published as the result, with retention or removal of the dispatched route decided by the frozen rule rather than after the fact.
- [hard] REQ-09: No measured or derived figure is copied into prose; each quantitative statement is a conclusion plus a pointer to the generated table row, receipt or ledger line that holds it.

## Notes

`dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md` and `dev/active/f547c394/protocol.md` are normative, and timed work runs only in a scheduled benchmark window. The canonical confirmation freezer is `dev/active/c7113c5a/survey/freeze-confirmation.py`; its family-description input carries the confirmation's own family prose.

title: Profile the production DVB-T2 bit interleaver
description:
Attribute the production DVB-T2 packed-bit scatter cost inside its real BICM consumers and issue a bounded materiality disposition without authorizing candidate implementation.

## Background

The repaired protocol-v3 re-measurement is accepted exploratory evidence: gf2 wins the whole packed-operation comparison, while conversion-subtracted 16-QAM cells leave a residual in which xdsopl's gather is faster. Earlier warm receipts remain withdrawn and cannot confirm the gap. This task rebuilds the current gf2 and xdsopl arms from exact pinned sources, profiles the actual `BitInterleaver::interleave` route used by the BICM harness and simulation stages, and attributes representation conversion, memory passes and scatter work. The result may nominate a concrete candidate only as input to an amended and re-reviewed breakdown.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A frozen protocol-v4 addendum and append-only family-ledger reservation predeclare Normal and Short FECFRAME paths for 16-QAM and 64-QAM, a streaming case, exploratory role, isolated and whole-consumer boundaries, cache states, conversion accounting, materiality rule, complexity budget and bounded search before timing.
- [hard] REQ-02: Scheduled benchmark-window execution produces an accepted exploratory receipt with exact rebuilt gf2 and xdsopl source, build and executable pins, raw paired samples, append-only execution log, checkpoints, runtime host provenance and durable negative or unavailable outcomes.
- [hard] REQ-03: The profile identifies the selected production route, BICM harness and simulation-stage consumers, call graph, hot instructions, allocation behavior, representation conversions, memory passes and isolated interleave cost beside whole-consumer cost.
- [hard] REQ-04: The disposition records the scatter as not material or nominates no more than two profile-supported branch-free or packed-word forms under the predeclared budget; withdrawn warm receipts remain historical context and do not confirm a candidate.
- [hard] REQ-05: A no-candidate or no-win disposition permits this profile to complete. If it nominates a material branch-free or packed-word form, this profile remains open until a planning-time Rust 1.95 compile and assembly record proves feasibility, including a runtime-gated scalar fallback for any capability-gated form, and the plan bracket is amended and re-reviewed to create the required candidate implementation and confirmation leaves, make them depend on this profile, and re-home publication behind their sinks in the instantiated dependency graph.

## Notes

The comparator remains xdsopl `PCTITL` for the ETSI bit-interleave operation. AFF3CT and circular shifts are not substitutes. Timed work runs only in a scheduled benchmark window.

Source references: [Etsi2015], [Xdsopl2026].

planning.outcome: DVB-T2 interleave materiality has a protocol-complete disposition

title: Publish the shift-permutation dispositions
description:
Publish generated story evidence that preserves family boundaries, negative results and each material candidate's completed evidence path without changing production code itself.

## Background

The report presents shifts, QC construction, generic puncturing and interleaving as separate workload families. It derives numeric statements from committed machine-readable artifacts, identifies actual production consumers, records QC runtime rotation as inapplicable, keeps the ETSI [Etsi2015] bit-interleave permutation distinct from the other interleavers, preserves the accepted AFF3CT [Cassagne2019] NR no-win while `prepare_llrs` is unchanged, and treats withdrawn DVB warm receipts against xdsopl `PCTITL` [Xdsopl2026] only as history. A family whose profile nominates no form ends at that profile. A family whose profile nominates a material form reaches this report only through the candidate implementation and confirmation leaves its nomination requires, and this report sits behind their terminal sinks in the dependency graph. The residual `BitVec` shift family is the one with such a path: its BMI2-gated funnel candidate carries the A/B confirmation whose outcome this report publishes, and the AVX2 lane-crossing funnel the same profile nominated is feasible at the MSRV, unselected for implementation in this epic, and preserved here as an outcome rather than dropped.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A deterministic generator reproduces the publication tables from committed receipts, profiles and content-pinned dispositions, including latency, throughput, whole-consumer costs, intervals, sample counts, conversion stages and runtime provenance where applicable.
- [hard] REQ-02: The findings map every story criterion to durable evidence and preserve the QC inapplicability, generic-puncturing separation, NR accepted no-win, unavailable mappings, withdrawn DVB evidence and profile no-win outcomes.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each family's disposition reaches this report through its own graph path: a profile nominating no form ends at that profile, while a material nomination's candidate implementation and confirmation work is complete and this report sits behind its terminal sink in the instantiated dependency graph.
- [hard] REQ-04: This report and the story stay open while a material nomination lacks its planning-time Rust 1.95 compile, assembly and scalar-fallback feasibility record, its reviewed amended manifest, its exact instantiated dependencies or its completed candidate evidence.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each performance claim cites its accepted receipt and protocol identity, while each absent comparison has an explicit semantic or consumer reason.
- [hard] REQ-06: The report states the residual-shift candidate's outcome as its confirmation's acceptance summary records it, qualifying or not, together with the retention decision the frozen rule produces, and records the nominated AVX2 lane-crossing funnel as feasible at the MSRV, not selected for implementation in this epic, and the reason for that selection.

## Notes

The report stays in the story's development area; permanent prose cites it rather than copying volatile measurements.

Source references: [Cassagne2019], [Etsi2015], [Xdsopl2026].
